question: A charge $q$ is moved from point A to point B on an equipotential surface. Why is the work done by the electric field in this process equal to zero?

options.A: Because the distance between A and B is negligible.
options.B: Because the electric field is perpendicular to the displacement at every point on the surface.
options.C: Because the electric field is zero everywhere on the surface.
options.D: Because the charge $q$ becomes zero on the surface.
